{
  "participants": [
    {
      "login": "Yudis-bit",
      "stance": "objection",
      "note": "noted that retrying pruneblockchain after a failed flush fails to delete files, and questioned block file reuse in FindNextBlockPos"
    },
    {
      "login": "nervana21",
      "stance": "support",
      "note": "Concept ACK"
    }
  ],
  "claims": [
    {
      "id": "rc:4457571575",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "correctness",
      "text": "Retrying pruneblockchain after a failed flush does not delete unlinked files because nSize is cleared and should_write remains false without a force flush",
      "quote": "If a flush fails after `PruneOneBlockFile()` clears `nSize`, retrying `pruneblockchain` won't clean up the files.",
      "clears_with": "change",
      "status": "answered",
      "status_note": "author explains this is deliberate: skipped writes are kept in memory until the next flush that writes deletes them",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:4634832807"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "rc:4634832807",
      "status_by_quote": "The files are still in `m_files_to_unlink` and the next flush that writes deletes them. That's deliberate on my part"
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:4457571582",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "question",
      "kind": "correctness",
      "text": "Whether it is possible for nFile to be in m_files_to_unlink in FindNextBlockPos",
      "quote": "Is it actually possible for `nFile` to be in `m_files_to_unlink` here?",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "answered",
      "status_note": "author explains how assumeutxo snapshot validation allows the file to be pruned and reused",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:4634911169"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "rc:4634911169",
      "status_by_quote": "Yes, after an assumeutxo snapshot validates."
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:4457571582",
      "part": 2,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "correctness",
      "text": "If an old file were reused in FindNextBlockPos, opening it with rb+ would overwrite the head without truncating existing data",
      "quote": "Also, if an old file were somehow reused here, opening it with `rb+` would overwrite the head without truncating the existing block data on disk.",
      "clears_with": "change",
      "status": "answered",
      "status_note": "author notes master has the same behavior and suggests addressing it in a followup PR",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:4634911169"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "rc:4634911169",
      "status_by_quote": "master reuses the file the same way after a failed prune flush... But I think that can be a fix in a separate / followup PR."
    }
  ],
  "support": [
    {
      "id": "c:6950454303",
      "verdict": "Concept ACK",
      "reason": "",
      "substantive": false,
      "evidence": "none",
      "areas": []
    }
  ],
  "notes": "Author pzafonte replied to all claims from Yudis-bit, explaining that delaying deletion until the next successful write is intentional, detailing the assumeutxo reuse mechanism, and suggesting the rb+ truncation issue be handled in a followup PR.",
  "waiting_on": [
    {
      "on": "reviewer",
      "what": "Yudis-bit to review author's explanations on retry behavior and file reuse",
      "id": "rc:4634911169"
    }
  ]
}

participants.note: noted that retrying pruneblockchain after a failed flush fails to delete files, and questioned block file reuse in FindNextBlockPos

claims.text: Retrying pruneblockchain after a failed flush does not delete unlinked files because nSize is cleared and should_write remains false without a force flush
claims.quote: If a flush fails after `PruneOneBlockFile()` clears `nSize`, retrying `pruneblockchain` won't clean up the files.
claims.status_note: author explains this is deliberate: skipped writes are kept in memory until the next flush that writes deletes them
claims.status_by_quote: The files are still in `m_files_to_unlink` and the next flush that writes deletes them. That's deliberate on my part

claims.text: Whether it is possible for nFile to be in m_files_to_unlink in FindNextBlockPos
claims.quote: Is it actually possible for `nFile` to be in `m_files_to_unlink` here?
claims.status_note: author explains how assumeutxo snapshot validation allows the file to be pruned and reused
claims.status_by_quote: Yes, after an assumeutxo snapshot validates.

claims.text: If an old file were reused in FindNextBlockPos, opening it with rb+ would overwrite the head without truncating existing data
claims.quote: Also, if an old file were somehow reused here, opening it with `rb+` would overwrite the head without truncating the existing block data on disk.
claims.status_note: author notes master has the same behavior and suggests addressing it in a followup PR
claims.status_by_quote: master reuses the file the same way after a failed prune flush... But I think that can be a fix in a separate / followup PR.

result.notes: Author pzafonte replied to all claims from Yudis-bit, explaining that delaying deletion until the next successful write is intentional, detailing the assumeutxo reuse mechanism, and suggesting the rb+ truncation issue be handled in a followup PR.

waiting_on.what: Yudis-bit to review author's explanations on retry behavior and file reuse
